candidates: Prefer `interface` over `type` aliases for all TypeScript type definitions; this is enforced by the `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-definitions` ESLint rule already configured in `.eslintrc.cjs`.

When typing a property or parameter that is always a single-field wrapper object (e.g., `{ actor: string }`), question whether the primitive type (e.g., `string`) can be used directly instead; accept the wrapper form only when the shape genuinely needs to vary or when flattening it would require cascading changes to the parser/jison layer.

Use the nullish-coalescing operator `??` rather than logical-OR `||` when supplying fallback values for expressions that may be `null` or `undefined`; `||` also coerces other falsy values such as `0` and `''`, which is rarely the intent.

When a function parameter is an object that callers may legitimately omit, model it as a default empty-object parameter with optional fields (e.g., `message: { text?: string; wrap?: boolean } = {}`) rather than marking the entire parameter optional (`message?:`); this removes the need to null-check the object reference throughout the function body.

Type local variables used as string-keyed dictionaries with an explicit `Record<KeyType, ValueType>` annotation (e.g., `const links: Record<string, string> = {}`) rather than leaving them as inferred `{}` or `object`.

Types shared across multiple files within a diagram package (e.g., `Actor`, `Message`, `Note`, `Box` in the sequence diagram) should be defined in a dedicated `types.ts` file inside that diagram directory and imported from there, rather than being defined inline in implementation files or duplicated across modules.
